A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching methods, experiments, and appendix structure. The complete text, equations, figures, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Figures 2 and 5 report original IsTree experiments training Transformers, Mamba RNNs, and hybrid models.

after.justification: Section 6 and Figures 2 and 5 retain original IsTree experiments, including revised hybrid-model results.

M1.justification: The regex-based retrieval procedure, hybrid architecture appending one Transformer layer, and CoT procedures remain unchanged. Definitions 3.5–3.6 and 5.5 and Algorithms 1–2 retain their substance.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same synthetic IsTree task. Figures 2 and 5 cover graphs with 16, 32, 64, and 128 nodes under vanilla, CoT, and retrieval conditions. No empirical dataset or task is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain LLaMA-style Transformers, Mamba RNNs, and Mamba with an additional LLaMA block. Their participation in the corresponding comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported settings remain unchanged: 0.5M/1M/2M models, 5,000 validation samples, final-iteration evaluation, half credit for missing predictions, and training with 1M samples or 5M upon nonconvergence. The revised hybrid scores are not accompanied by a stated protocol change.

E4.justification: Figure 5 revises the existing analysis of whether hybrid models need CoT or retrieval and how performance scales with graph size. The replacement evidence shows weak vanilla performance and declining CoT accuracy for smaller hybrids at 128 nodes. No additional analysis conditions are introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars for these experiments. Statistical reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Under unchanged reported settings, Figure 5 replaces approximately 100% vanilla hybrid accuracy with roughly 50%. At 128 nodes, CoT accuracy for the 0.5M and 1M hybrids changes from near-perfect to approximately 75–77%. Section 6 replaces the finding that hybrids perform best even without CoT with performance on par with Transformers. Figure 2's results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 5.7 loses its special-case guarantee that a hybrid RNN solves the binary-sequence-derived IsTree problem without CoT. Appendix B.12 removes the corresponding constructive proof. The general O(n log n) CoT guarantee and the remaining mathematical results are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims: CoT improves RNN expressiveness but leaves a retrieval bottleneck, while explicit retrieval or one appended Transformer layer closes the polynomial-time representation gap with CoT.

C2.justification: Section 6 no longer interprets hybrid models as superior and successful without CoT; it interprets their revised performance as matching Transformers and supporting the retained theory. Section 3 explicitly extends the applicability discussion to finite-KV-cache architectures. The stated practical and training/generalization limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Both provide the same code link, graph and CoT generation algorithms, frozen tied embeddings, RoPE, Adam/cosine schedule, and learning rates. No additional implementation, hardware, runtime, or resource-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: v3 adds Gu et al. (2022) on structured state spaces and Oren et al. (2024), Transformers Are Multi-State RNNs. It expands the introductory background and clarifies its relationship to Yang et al.'s concurrent CoT expressiveness results without substantially changing its positioning.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites portions of the introduction and related work, removes the duplicated Chain of Thought paragraph, clarifies the comparison-without-CoT heading, and makes small wording corrections. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: The same five figures remain. Figures 2 and 5 lose grid lines, Figure 5's caption drops the universal near-perfect-accuracy statement, and citations and cross-references become blue links. Text and figures reflow within the existing layout.

improvement.justification: Removing duplicated prose and adding context improve readability. However, v3 replaces the hybrid model's near-perfect no-CoT results with chance-level results and withdraws the associated theorem claim and proof without explaining the discrepancy. The PDFs do not establish whether these substantive revisions correct earlier errors or reflect an undocumented experimental difference, so their net effect on scientific quality remains uncertain.
